biomarker_name.evidence_quote: High-dose MTX significantly decreased the Bacteroidetes phylum. MTX altered 14 bacterial genera and 81 amplicon sequence variants (ASVs). Changes in gut bacterial taxa and gene family abundance were distinct between responders and non-responders.
biomarker_name.notes: Multiple biomarkers identified across microbiota composition, gene function, and immune parameters.

biomarker_unit.evidence_quote: MTX-R exhibited a significant decrease in Bacteroidetes relative to MTX-NR. 7 immunocyte populations were significantly lower and 1 was significantly higher in the post-MTX recipients. Fold change percentage in which values are normalized to the pre-MTX group.
biomarker_unit.notes: Various units used depending on biomarker type.

value: ANOSIM R=0.60 to 0.75 for community structure changes
DESeq p adj=0.001 for Bacteroidetes decrease
biomarker_value.evidence_quote: MTX significantly altered gut microbial community structure (ANOSIM, R=0.60, p=0.006 after 1 day; R=0.75, p=0.006 final day). High-dose MTX significantly decreased Bacteroidetes (DESeq p adj=0.001). 7 immunocyte populations significantly lower in post-MTX recipients (range: 0.64–1.33 fold change).
biomarker_value.notes: Values reflect various statistical measures including ANOSIM, DESeq p-values, fold changes, and clinical response criteria.

disease_response_os.notes: This study is focused on rheumatoid arthritis treatment response, not cancer survival or overall survival metrics.

disease_response_os_unit.notes: Not applicable; OS not measured in this study.

ecog_performance_status.notes: ECOG performance status not reported for study participants.

value: Decreased richness in ex vivo communities
feces_phenotype_value.evidence_quote: High-dose MTX significantly decreased the Bacteroidetes phylum and altered 14 bacterial genera. Consistent with our studies in mice and on isolates, Bacteroidetes decreased and Actinobacteria increased. MTX significantly impaired the growth of these complex microbial communities.
feces_phenotype_value.notes: Multiple fecal microbiota phenotypes reported across different experimental conditions.

tumor_size_measurement.notes: Not applicable; this study focuses on rheumatoid arthritis, not cancer with tumor measurements.

tumor_size_residual_measurement.notes: Not applicable; no tumor treatment endpoints measured.

value: Study used gnotobiotic mice colonized with human donor microbiota
MTX doses: 1 mg/kg (low) and 50 mg/kg (high) in mice
Human RA patients received oral MTX at standard care doses
Baseline and 1 month post-MTX treatment samples collected
Responder defined as DAS28 decrease ≥1.8 plus continued MTX use
16S rRNA gene sequencing performed on fecal, ileal, cecal, and colon samples
DSS (dextran sodium sulfate) used as inflammatory trigger in mouse experiments
Flow cytometry used to assess immune cell populations
45 bacterial isolates from 6 phyla tested for MTX sensitivity
uncurated_metadata.evidence_quote: Germ-free mice were colonized with stool from human donors. Mice were treated either with saline/PBS, MTX 1 mg/kg or 50 mg/kg daily. Consecutive patients from NYU Langone's rheumatology clinics were screened. Clinical responder status was defined a priori as DAS28 score improved by at least 1.8. Stool samples were collected at baseline and 1 month after MTX initiation.
uncurated_metadata.notes: Comprehensive study design combining in vitro isolate studies, gnotobiotic mouse models, ex vivo patient stool experiments, and longitudinal patient samples.

host_species.evidence_quote: C57BL/6J mice (females, ages 6–16 weeks) were obtained from the UCSF Gnotobiotics core facility. Consecutive patients from the New York University Langone Medical Center's rheumatology clinics and offices were screened for the presence of RA.
host_species.section: Methods — Experimental Model and Subject Details
host_species.notes: Study includes both human (Homo sapiens) RA patients and mice (Mus musculus) colonized with human microbiota.
